description: Survey finds strong interest in AI among teachers, but gaps in training, infrastructure and student-data safeguards could hamper responsible adoption in classrooms.
body_lead: Government-school teachers in Karnataka are increasingly using artificial intelligence (AI) as a teaching aid, but gaps in training, digital infrastructure and data-privacy safeguards could pose challenges to wider adoption, according to a new survey by JanAI, an initiative of Head Held High Foundation. The survey covered 797 government-school teachers across Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Maharashtra, with Karnataka accounting for 134 responses. About 63 percent of respondents from Karnataka were from rural schools, while 24 percent were from urban schools.
